## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle *yīnyì* 音義 (phonological-semantic glossary) on the One-Syllable Crown-Wheel-King ritual manuals by **Amoghavajra** ([不空](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%8D%E7%A9%BA)). The *yīnyì* genre — pronunciation and semantic glossing of obscure terms — is a Táng Chinese Buddhist scholarly tradition particularly important for Esoteric texts, where Sanskrit transliterations and *bīja*-syllables require special phonetic attention.

**Abstract**

The text glosses the technical terms, Sanskrit transliterations, and *bīja*-syllables in the One-Syllable Crown-Wheel-King ritual manuals ([KR6j0124](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0124), [KR6j0130](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0130), [KR6j0132](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0132), [KR6j0134](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0134)). It is a working philological reference for practitioners of these ritual texts. The composition dates from Amoghavajra's mature Cháng'ān period (746–774).
